Big banks opened Q3 season: Goldman crushed it ($17.01 EPS vs ~$13.65 est), while JPMorgan missed (~$5.57 vs ~$5.90). Gold firmed toward ~$4,185–4,200. The scanner boarded two names into this split tape — validate both hard at 9:35.
focus.notdown: GameStop (GME) is the scanner’s bullish boarded breakout — it closed at a fresh 52-week high (~$27.23) on 1.83x volume, driven by heavy insider buying (Cohen +700K shares) and a Yorkville/Ives $32 outperform initiation, and the breakout has held one full session above the ~$26.53 pivot. But a bear call on a double-beat is counter-intuitive; the move is small and volume is light. Chip/semis are falling hard, but shorting into an earnings-week VIX uptick risks a violent snap-back. On a RED day, the disciplined answer is to sell nothing new unless it’s a validated setup at reduced size.
focus.why: Why RED? Composite ~46 sits at the top of MILD and P(≥1% gap) at ~36% is just above the 35% trigger — the gap trigger alone locks out GREEN. More important than the numbers: a live chip sell-off plus the first big-bank earnings cluster (mixed: GS beat, JPM missed) stacked on a 5%+ bond market and ongoing Hormuz attacks is an open-ended, two-sided tail. The scanner boarded two names — DPZ (bearish Type A · B+) and GME (bullish Type C · B+) — but one is a counter-intuitive double-beat fade and the other a thin meme breakout gapping down pre-market. Trade only validated setups at reduced size, or stand down. Cash is a position today.

setups.read: Domino’s (DPZ) is the scanner’s one boarded post-earnings gap — and it’s a bearish Type A, which is counter-intuitive on a double beat. DPZ reported Q3 pre-market: EPS $4.60 vs ~$4.36 (a ~4.2% beat) and revenue $1.186B vs ~$1.17B — a genuine double-beat — yet the stock slipped because U.S. same-store sales grew just 0.3% (near-flat comps), so the market faded the print toward ~$304 from Monday’s ~$310.90 close (a ~2% gap down). Three honest cautions (voiced here, not by dropping the row): (1) the options-implied move was ~5.6% but the realized gap was only ~2.1%, so the move is small and could reverse; (2) relative volume is just ~0.05x — far below the 1.3x confirmation bar, the single biggest red flag; and (3) the S/R stack above price is tight (swing ~$304.99, gap floor ~$310.90, swing ~$318.57). Next earnings ~Jan 2027 is outside DTE. On a RED day with sub-1.3x volume on a double-beat fade, this is strictly 4-VAL-at-9:35 territory — quarter-to-half size, skip if it reclaims green.
setups.check_note: Bearish 4-VAL at 9:35: need price < $310.90 (gap holding down), < today’s open, and in the lower third of range. Volume ~0.05x is WAY below the 1.3x bar — this is the key disqualifier to respect; a double-beat that fails to confirm down can snap back up. Short call above the ~$310.90 gap floor; size down hard and skip if volume stays thin or it opens green.

setups.read: GameStop (GME) is the scanner’s bullish boarded breakout — it pushed to a fresh 52-week high (~$27.25, pivot ~$26.53) and closed at ~$27.23 on 1.83x the 50-day volume, riding heavy insider buying (Cohen +700K shares at ~$24.41) and a fresh Yorkville/Ives $32 outperform initiation. Crucially, the breakout has HELD one full session above the pivot — stronger than a same-day breakout, with more S/R behind the strike. Liquidity passes (OI ~14,363 on the ATM chain, spread $0.06). Honest cautions: (1) pre-market it’s gapping slightly down ~$27.06–27.09 (~−0.5%), just below Monday’s close, so confirm it holds; (2) only 1 S/R layer (the pivot ~$26.53, −2.1%); (3) it’s a thin, overbought meme name with a late-October warrant overhang. Next earnings ~Dec 8 is outside DTE. On a RED day, this is 4-VAL-at-9:35 territory — half size at most, skip if it opens red.
setups.check_note: Bullish 4-VAL at 9:35: need price > $27.23 (gap holding), > today’s open, and in the upper third of range — AND holding above the ~$26.53 pivot. Pre-market it’s gapping slightly down ~$27.06, so it currently FAILS check #1; do not enter unless it reclaims the prior close. Held-1-session breakout is a plus, but it’s a meme name into a RED tape — size down; short put at/below the $26.53 pivot.

risks: Chip / semiconductor sell-off — a deepening rout in memory names (MU, SNDK, WDC, SK Hynix) is dragging Nasdaq futures ~−0.7% and could spill into the broad tape. This is today’s most active single-sector risk to watch.

Big-bank earnings (mixed) — JPMorgan missed (~$5.57 EPS vs ~$5.90) while Goldman crushed it ($17.01 vs ~$13.65); Wells Fargo and Citi also reported. Divergent reactions can whipsaw financials and set the tone for Q3 season.

CPI / PPI inflation watch — with the 10Y near 24-year highs (though easing to ~5.19% today) and sticky Dec-hike odds (~69%), a hot inflation print this week stacked on the oil backdrop would be the worst-case macro combination.

Strait of Hormuz attacks — fresh tanker incidents keep Brent above $100 even as Russian-diesel hopes ease prices. Roughly a fifth of the world’s oil moves through it; any escalation sends crude (and jet fuel) vertical.

DPZ follow-through risk — a double-beat that faded on flat comps on ~0.05x volume is an unconfirmed, two-sided move; a reversal back up would squeeze any bear-call entry. Respect the sub-1.3x volume flag.

Q3 season opened this morning: the big banks (JPM, Goldman, Wells Fargo, Citi) reported — GS beat big, JPM missed. Two names boarded today: DPZ (reported pre-market, a bearish Type A) and GME (Type C breakout, next print ~Dec 8, outside DTE). For everything else, keep every spread clear of its name’s print and short-dated enough to clear the data.
